title: microchunk-affinity: block-granularity KV allocator with incremental compaction for GPU paging
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Current paged KV cache uses coarse page eviction which causes low packing efficiency for mixed-size KV entries (short KV tokens vs long context blobs). This amplifies GPU memory pressure and triggers expensive whole-page GPU swap-outs, increasing tail latency during continuous batching. We need an allocator and runtime policy that reduces full-page writebacks and improves hotset locality while preserving predictable eviction behavior for SLOs.

Proposal summary: Implement a microchunk-affinity allocator: split each logical 64KB page into fixed 4KB microchunks (configurable). Track per-microchunk residency, hotness score, and token-affinity vectors to co-locate frequently-accessed microchunks. Add an incremental compactor that merges and compacts live microchunks into contiguous page frames on the GPU, allowing sparse pages to be reclaimed without full-page swap. Integrate compaction with batching signals so that compaction occurs opportunistically during low-latency windows or background CPU/GPU cycles.

Key behaviors: compact partial pages asynchronously, prefer compaction over full-page eviction when reclaimed bytes >= threshold (default 25% of page). Evict cold microchunks first; perform atomic pointer swaps for KV metadata to avoid long pauses. Keep KV access APIs unchanged; allocator and residency manager are transparent to callers.

Design goals: reduce GPU swap frequency, minimize p95 generation latency spikes by avoiding full-page writebacks in critical paths, improve packing efficiency for small KV items, and keep metadata memory overhead under 3% of total KV bytes.

Trade-offs: additional metadata and bookkeeping for microchunks increases CPU load and memory. Compaction work consumes GPU cycles (but can be scheduled on spare capacity or lower-priority CUDA streams). Complexity increases testing and failure modes.

Open questions: optimal microchunk size for median workloads, how to tune compaction thresholds per model family, interactions with quantized model memory layouts (alignment constraints), and fallback behavior under extreme oversubscription.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate >=35% reduction in average bytes swapped to host under mixed small/large KV workloads compared to baseline (no microchunk compaction)
p95 latency during steady-state continuous-batching should not regress more than 3% for LLM-13B sized models
Metadata memory overhead < 3% at peak residency
No observable increase in OOM events after 72h soak test under 2x traffic
design_notes: Microchunk size: default 4KB, parameterizable per deployment. Rationale: balances TLB alignment (4KB native) and metadata granularity for small KV entries.
Residency map: bitset per page where each bit maps to a microchunk; store in host pinned memory for fast scans.
Hotness scoring: combine last-access timestamp (coarse) and batched-access counters; decay factor configurable per cycle.
Compaction algorithm: scan pages with spare live density < 75%, schedule GPU DMA to copy live microchunks into destination page frames, update pointer table atomically, mark source microchunks free.
Backpressure: if compaction queue > threshold, stop background compaction and fall back to eviction to preserve latency SLOs.
Alignment: destination pages must preserve model-required alignment (8/16/32 byte) — compaction must respect internal tensor packing boundaries.
Interplay with continuous batching: use batch boundary hooks to pin microchunks touched by in-flight batches to avoid moving during generation; compaction skips pinned microchunks.
Failure modes: partial compaction failure should roll back atomic pointer swaps and retry later; add metrics for compaction retries and aborts.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): build feature gated by runtime flag on staging cluster (1 node), enable microchunk residency only + observability, no compaction
Phase 1 (background compaction): enable compaction on non-critical pods during off-peak windows; run 48h soak, collect swap/latency metrics
Phase 2 (controlled traffic): enable on 10% of traffic for production clusters with conservative thresholds; expand to 50% after 7 days if metrics stable
Phase 3 (default): enable for all clusters with tuned thresholds and automated scaling rules
test_plan: Unit tests for microchunk bitset operations, pointer swap atomicity, and compaction rollback
Integration tests: synthetic workloads mixing 1–16 token KV items and large context blobs to validate packing improvements
Performance jobs: run long-running continuous-batching generator with 100qps for 72h to observe swap/writeback patterns
Chaos tests: kill compaction worker mid-copy to ensure recovery and no corruption
Regression tests against existing eviction protocol ensuring identical exposure on KV API
metrics_targets: Swap bytes/sec: -35% vs baseline on mixed workload
Average compaction time per page < 12ms for 64KB pages on T4-equivalent GPU
Compaction GPU cycles consumed < 5% of peak inference GPU utilization during normal load
comments: 2026-02-22 — Aisha Raman: Initial write-up and simulation results attached to Confluence. Sim shows ~42% swap reduction for synthetic small-item heavy workload.
2026-03-01 — Carlos Mendoza: Prototype allocator implemented; needs atomic pointer swap API review. Observed metadata overhead ~2.6% in integration run.
2026-03-05 — Design review notes: PM suggests adding per-customer thresholds; agreed to add config knobs in control plane.
2026-03-10 — QA: Running chaos tests; found edge case when compaction queue flush intersects with on-demand eviction. Added guard to drain compaction queue before eviction of destination frame.
2026-03-12 — Eng lead: Approving Phase 0 canary. Feature flag GA name: runtime.kv.microchunk_compaction_enabled. Next action: PR for observability metrics (compaction.duration, compaction.aborts).
